data.mechanism: AMPK can promote the clearance of damaged mitochondria, in part by phosphorylating ULK1: cells whose ULK1 cannot be phosphorylated by AMPK show defective mitophagy under starvation. How much AMPK contributes depends on the cell type and on the kind of energy stress.
data.mechanism_beginner: The cell's energy sensor can help clear out damaged mitochondria, partly by switching on an autophagy starter kinase. How much it matters depends on the cell and on the kind of stress.
data.boundary: Two studies of different kinds: EGA2010 (cells and C. elegans, AMPK-site mutant of ULK1) and ZHU2026 (mouse toxicology model, where LKB1/AMPK loss also went with mitochondrial DNA leakage and liver inflammation; that downstream link is shown only there). The upstream step is disputed: PAR2023 (Park, Lee and Kim, Nat Commun 2023, PMID 37225695, in this corpus) reports that under glucose starvation and mitochondrial energy stress AMPK restrains ULK1 activation and autophagy induction; see AMPK-ULK1, where it is recorded as the conflicting study. PAR2023 measured ULK1 activity, bulk autophagy and aggrephagy rather than mitophagy itself, so it bears on the upstream step and not directly on the mitophagy readout here.
